en.html:
I had never supposed it could be accomplished overnight.

Even a gifted warrior might devote his entire life to training and still need fortune's assistance to reach that state. Had Kageaki Minato obtained one clue at this age, it would have been luck beyond expectation.

But one clue was not my requirement. Everything was required. Necessary, therefore it had to be obtained. Such was my position.

Think of it that way...
After two hours with not the slightest sense of progress, how was I to avoid feeling thoroughly bleak?

en.text:
Impatience brought no benefit.
Neither, naturally, did giving up.

One more attempt.
This time—◆that leaf would do.

Shaken by the breeze, it looked ready to fall. Without eyes or ears, I would perceive the instant it fell and catch it before it reached the ground.

en.html:
Kageaki"Discard every attachment. Desire nothing, seek nothing... Make the mind emptyempty, and become one with the world, I believe."
童心"Emptiness leads to the Allwhole. He who would obtain everything must discard everything."
Kageaki"Yes."
童心"Form is emptiness; emptiness is form. Ten thousand things exist, yet not one thing to cling to..."
Kageaki"..."
童心"Do you not see?"
Kageaki"...Sir?"
童心"You seek no-thought in order to fight somebody, yes?"
Kageaki"Yes."
童心"There is your attachment, sitting in plain view."
Kageaki"————"
童心"Because you cling to victory... you seek a state only reached by discarding attachment."
童心"That reasoning cannot pass, surely."
Kageaki"........................"
童心"So long as winning matters, no-thought remains beyond you. Reach no-thought, and winning no longer matters."
童心"Regrettably, then—your training to obtain no-thought and defeat your enemy has absolutely, entirely, no purpose!"
童心"Hwahahahahahahahahaha!!"

童心"Well now, what am I doing? Faced with such honesty, leaving after merely laughing becomes uncomfortable..."

童心"Young man, what you should seek is not no-thought. No-self, perhaps."
Kageaki"No-self."
童心"Yes."
Kageaki"..."
童心"You understand the meaning?"
Kageaki"Following the literal sense... reducing the entirety of one's selfself to nothing."
童心"Exactly. If no-thought makes nothing of the outer universeworld, no-self makes nothing of the inner universeself."
童心"Another way that leads to the Allwhole."
Kageaki"But, Reverend sir."
童心"Yes."
Kageaki"Would this not be equally meaningless for me...?"

en.html:
童心"Truly, private desire alone?"
Kageaki"Well..."
Muramasa"...I will not explain the details, but the opponent causes various difficulties. Defeating them would be better for the world."
Kageaki"Muramasa—"
Muramasa"Naturally, I have no intention of claiming that makes us righteous. Such presumption would be absurd."
童心"No, no. Precisely that presumption is important here."
童心"Young man. Because your fight is first a private matter, you are ashamed to call it service to the world... But that also is a misunderstanding."
Kageaki"...How so?"
童心"Attain no-self, and neither private business nor private desire remains."
童心"Only the world's greater cause. Only the world's will, desiring that enemy's destruction."
Kageaki"————"
童心"If even a fragment of a greater cause belongs to your struggle, do not hesitate. Seek no-self."
童心"Even when your will disappears... the world's will shall drive you forward and strike down your enemy."
Muramasa"............"
童心"............"
童心"Huh, huhuh. Well, words entirely unsuited to me."
童心"Become such a warrior of the greater cause, and the first man cut down would be this precept-breaking monk. Digging my own grave, that is what we call it."
童心"Young man, do not become such a person! It would inconvenience me enormously!"
童心"Hahahahahahahahaha!!"
